3. The petitioners as defendants appeared in the suit and filed an application under Order 7, rule 11 (d) of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) for rejection of the plaint contending, inter that a reading of the plaint apparently showed that the plaintiff based its claim for realization of compensation from the defendants relying on the facts which occurred in between the period from 1992-1994 i.e. more than 12 years before filing of the suit and therefore, the suit was barred by limitation under articles 60-62 and 115 of the Limitation Act (the Act) and, as such, the plaint was liable to be rejected. 

 4. The said application was contested by the plaintiff-opposite party by filing a written objection contending that the suit was very much filed within time from the last date of the cause of action, so the same was not barred by limitation. 

 5. The defendant-petitioners also filed a written objection against the objection filed by the plaintiff reasserting that the suit was barred by limitation. 

 7. Mr. Shamim Khaled Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners by placing the plaint which has been annexed to the revision application as annexure-‘A’ submitted that the plaint if read as, a whole it would appear that the suit is barred by limitation, under articles 64, 65 and 115 of the Act as the same has been filed relying on the facts which occurred during the period 1992-1994 and, as such, the learned Joint District Judge committed error of law in passing the impugned order in not rejecting the plaint which has occasioned failure of justice. Mr. Shamim Khaled further submitted that although in the plaint the last cause of action for filing the suit has been shown as on 5.4.2003 when the alleged legal notice was given to the defendant to pay them the compensation yet in fact the plaintiffs claim of compensation being based on the facts which allegedly occurred during the period 1992-1994, that is, much prior to 2003 as apparent from a plain reading of the plaint, the suit was barred by limitation, So the plaint was liable to be rejected, but the learned Joint District Judge on an erroneous approach to the case passed the impugned order refusing to reject the plaint and, as such, the same calls for interference by this court. 

 8. Mr. Md. Nazrul Islam, the learned advocate appearing for the plaintiff-opposite party, on the other hand, submitted that the suit was filed by the plaintiff for realization of money and to show the foundation of its claim the occurrence which occurred between the parties during the period from 1992-1994 upto the culmination of the last date of the cause of action to file the suit were mentioned and in the plaint it having been categorically stated' that the plaintiff was not aware about those facts earlier, the suit cannot be said to be barred by limitation, and, therefore, the' court below rightly refused to reject the plaint. Mr. Nazrul Islam further submitted that in the plaint it has been categorically stated that although the plaintiff gave a legal notice to the defendants on 5.4.2003 asking them to pay it the compensation yet in-spite of the receipt of the said notice the defendants did not reply to the same and the suit having been filed on 24.1.2006 that is, were within the period of 3 (three) years from 5.4.2003 the question for the suit being barred by limitation does not arise at all, the learned Joint District Judge rightly rejected the application filed by the defendants under order 7, rule 11(d) of the Code and, as such, no interference is called for by this court with the impugned order and consequently the rule is liable to be discharged. 

 9. The plaint which has been annexed to the revision application is a very lengthy one, being 69 pages, yet we have gone through the same. It is a fact that in the plaint some facts have been stated which occurred in the years 1992-1994. But it appeared to us that those have been stated to show as to how things proceeded upto the culmination of the last date of the cause of action to file the suit for compensation from the defendants. In the plaint it has been categorically stated that the plaintiff did not know about, those facts earlier. It further appeared that the plaintiff gave legal notice to the defendants on 5.4.2003 claiming compensation from them which though was received by them on 6.4.2003, yet they choose not to reply to the same. Along with the plaint schedule of the claim has been given, From schedule 'Kha' to the plaint it appeared that some of the plaintiff s claim accrued in the years 2003, 2004 and 2004, so those are definitely within the period of 3 (three) years from the date of the last cause of action, therefore, it cannot straight way be said that the entire claim of the plaintiff is barred by limitation as contended by Mr. Shamim Khaled Ahmed. Whether the plaintiff can rely or base upon the facts which occurred during the period 1992-94 for its claim of compensation from the defendant which it made lastly by legal notice dated 5.4.2003 or not is purely a question of fact and can only be decided after the sifting of the evidence to be adduced by the parties, particularly limitation being a mixed question of fact and law. In view of the above, we do not find any error committed by the court below in passing the impugned order occasioning failure of justice rejecting the application filed by the defendants under order 7, Rule 11(d) of the Code, therefore, no interference is called for by this court with the impugned order. However, we make it very clear that the point as argued by Mr. Shamim Khaled Ahmed, can very much be agitated at the time of final hearing of the suit by framing a specific issue to the effect "whether the claim of the plaintiff is barred by limitation."
